papers.title: A systems biology network analysis of root resorption biomarkers and their clinical relevance in orthodontics: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: External apical root resorption is a frequently reported iatrogenic consequence of orthodontic tooth movement. This pilot study used an integrated systems biology approach to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers associated with orthodontic root resorption to support future functional research.
papers.summary: This pilot study applies systems biology network analysis to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers associated with external apical root resorption during orthodontic treatment. The findings aim to guide future functional research into this common iatrogenic side effect of orthodontic tooth movement.

papers.title: Harnessing computational intelligence for synthetic lethality: A roadmap from network biology to interpretable deep learning in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Synthetic lethality (SL) is an emerging therapeutic paradigm in precision oncology that enables the selective targeting of cancer cells based on their specific genetic vulnerabilities. Despite its clinical promise, the enormous combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions poses a major challenge for experimental screening. This review provides a critical survey of computational SL discovery, moving beyond sequential descriptions to offer a comparative synthesis of architectures ranging from traditional network-based models to advanced graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. W
papers.summary: This review surveys computational methods for predicting synthetic lethality in cancer, comparing traditional network-based models with modern deep learning approaches like graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. It argues that interpretable deep learning can help navigate the vast combinatorial space of gene-gene interactions and accelerate the identification of therapeutic targets in precision oncology.

papers.title: Enterobacteriaceae for succinic acid biomanufacturing: metabolic blueprints, systems-level engineering and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Succinic acid (SA) is a key C4 platform molecule with wide industrial relevance, including bio-based polymers and solvents. Current reviews largely emphasize traditional producers (e.g., Actinobacillus, Mannheimia, and Basfia) and rarely synthesize progress in Enterobacteriaceae. Here, we close this gap by providing a systems-level review of SA biomanufacturing in Enterobacteriaceae, focusing on non-model genera (Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter) that combine fast growth, facultative anaerobiosis, broad feedstock utilization, and high engineering amenability. We outline the metabolic blue
papers.summary: This review synthesizes progress in engineering Enterobacteriaceae (Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter) for succinic acid biomanufacturing, highlighting their advantages over traditional producers like Actinobacillus and Mannheimia. It covers metabolic blueprints, systems-level engineering strategies, and future perspectives for these non-model organisms.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover and interpret functional modules. It addresses the limitations of existing module discovery methods by providing direct biological interpretability and reducing redundancy compared to pathway-based approaches. The tool enables researchers to translate complex molecular signatures into coherent functional insights.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined how the expression of protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relates to semen quality in rams, analyzing 15 ejaculates from five animals. The authors found that protamine gene expression is associated with total sperm motility, and they used gene regulatory network analysis to propose potential upstream regulators of these genes.

papers.title: KBase: Open-source Platform for Collaborative Biological Data Analysis and Publication.
papers.abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy's Systems Biology Knowledgebase (KBase; www.kbase.us) is an open, collaborative platform that integrates data, models, and analysis tools to accelerate discovery in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recently, KBase expanded as a comprehensive, multi-omics ecosystem. KBase enables representation of scientific samples, long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, and scalable modeling of microbial communities across diverse environments. KBase also generates digital notebooks as citable, executable research objects that link data
papers.summary: KBase is an open-source, collaborative platform that integrates multi-omics data, models, and analysis tools to support research in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recent expansions add long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, scalable microbial community modeling, and executable digital notebooks that serve as citable research objects linking data and analyses.

papers.title: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference depends on high-quality prior knowledge, yet curated priors are often incomplete or unavailable across species and cell types. We present GLM-Prior, a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions from nucleotide sequence. We integrate GLM-Prior with PMF-GRN in a dual-stage pipeline that combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression data for prior-conditioned GRN inference. Across six cell-line contexts, GLM-Prior performance scales with positive label abundance and TF coverage, showing above-chance a
papers.summary: GLM-Prior is a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions directly from nucleotide sequence, providing transferable prior knowledge for gene regulatory network inference. Integrated with PMF-GRN in a dual-stage pipeline, it combines these sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression data to infer GRNs across cell types and species where curated priors are unavailable. Performance scales with positive label abundance and TF coverage, outperforming chance across six cell-line contexts.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Host Regulatory and Immune Networks with Inferred Dysbiosis Relevance in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence suggests that intestinal microbial dysbiosis contributes to colorectal tumorigenesis by reshaping host molecular signaling and the tumor immune microenvironment. However, the molecular mechanisms linking microbiome-associated alterations to host regulatory networks and disease progression remain incompletely understood. Objective: This study aimed to identify the microbiome-associated molecular regulators and immune modulators involved in colorectal cancer through an
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify host regulatory and immune networks in colorectal cancer that are associated with inferred microbial dysbiosis. The authors link microbiome-related alterations to specific molecular regulators and immune modulators, suggesting mechanisms by which dysbiosis may shape the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Integrated Cell-Based Transcriptomic and Pathway Profiling Enables Scalable Functional Screening of Bioactive Microalgal Extracts.
papers.abstract: Background: Microalgae and cyanobacteria represent a largely unexplored source of bioactive compounds, but systematic screening of extensive strain collections is limited by the cost and complexity of conventional chemical and pharmacological characterization. Here, we evaluated a scalable functional screening strategy integrating human cell-based gene expression profiling, quantitative molecular pathway analysis, and direct cytotoxicity testing to prioritize bioactive microalgal and cyanobacterial extracts for subsequent investigation. Results: Forty-eight extracts were screened using HL-60 h
papers.summary: This study presents a scalable functional screening pipeline that combines human cell-based transcriptomic profiling, pathway analysis, and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize bioactive compounds from microalgae and cyanobacteria. Screening 48 extracts in HL-60 cells demonstrates that integrated gene expression and pathway profiling can efficiently triage complex natural product mixtures for further investigation.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational systems-biology method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize drug combinations that could overcome primary non-response to targeted therapies. By identifying and reversing non-response signatures, the approach narrows the vast space of possible drug pairs into a ranked set of promising combination therapies.

papers.title: A Human Accelerated Region Drives Opposing Heterochronic Changes in Craniofacial and Limb Development.
papers.abstract: Many human developmental processes proceed over a prolonged timescale compared to other primates, a phenomenon known as heterochrony. Human accelerated regions (HARs), which encode transcriptional enhancers with human-specific activity, have been implicated in the evolution of novel human traits. However, their contributions to changes in developmental timing remain unknown. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing and developmental trajectory analyses in a genetically humanized mouse model of the HAR HACNS1 , we show that HACNS1 drives heterochronic shifts in opposite directions during craniofacia
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using a humanized mouse model of the human accelerated region HACNS1, the authors show that this enhancer drives opposite heterochronic shifts in craniofacial versus limb development. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and developmental trajectory analyses reveal that HACNS1 alters developmental timing in a tissue-specific manner, linking human-specific enhancer activity to evolutionary changes in developmental pace.

papers.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Gene-Network Analysis Prioritise a TREM2/LGALS3/GPNMB Scar-Associated Macrophage Programme in Human Liver Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: Macrophages organise the fibrotic niche of liver cirrhosis. The scar-associated macrophage state is well described, but the genes that define it have rarely been ranked in an unbiased, model-based way, and the statistical limits of such re-analyses are seldom reported. Here we set out to re-derive the scar-associated macrophage programme without supervision, to rank its constituent genes by convergent computational evidence, and to state explicitly what a cohort of this size can and cannot support. We re-analysed 58,358 single-cell transcriptomes from five uninjured and five cirrhotic human li
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed 58,358 single-cell transcriptomes from healthy and cirrhotic human livers using explainable AI and gene-network methods to unbiasedly rank genes defining scar-associated macrophages. They converge on a TREM2/LGALS3/GPNMB programme and explicitly report the statistical limits of such re-analyses given the cohort size.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a minimal three-gene network combining a toggle switch and repressilator, to show that a single circuit can simultaneously exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors like oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a 'zoo' of multifunctional dynamics and assess their robustness. The work challenges the traditional separation of studying these behaviors in isolation and provides a framework for classifying emergent circuit behaviors.

papers.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa
papers.summary: The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and, crucially, for evaluating the structural accuracy of the inferred networks against known causal gene-gene relationships. This addresses a gap in available software for both Bayesian network inference and causal validation in single-cell GRN analysis.

papers.title: Bayesian inference of gene regulatory networks at stochastic steady state.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) form the regulatory backbone that coordinates gene expression. The architecture of GRNs shapes their function and constrains the biochemical pathways through which information flows. Inferring the structure of regulatory interactions is thus essential for understanding biological systems and designing targeted therapies. Despite substantial progress in GRN inference, most approaches-from statistical methods to deep learning-do not take into account fundamental biochemical processes that drive regulatory dynamics. To address this shortcoming, here, we present a n
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: The authors present a Bayesian method for inferring gene regulatory network structure that explicitly models the underlying biochemical processes driving regulatory dynamics, rather than treating network inference as a purely statistical or black-box machine learning problem. By leveraging stochastic steady-state assumptions, the approach aims to recover more biologically faithful network architectures from gene expression data.

papers.title: Sphingolipid Remodeling in Colorectal Cancer Reveals a Continuum-like Metabolic Organization.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits substantial metabolic heterogeneity, but the organization of sphingolipid remodeling remains incompletely understood. In this exploratory single-center study, we integrated patient-matched tissue lipidomics, systemic oxidative stress profiling, and independent transcriptomic analyses. Tumor tissue, adjacent non-neoplastic mucosa, and preoperative serum were collected from 40 patients with CRC, with serum obtained from 23 hospitalized non-cancer controls. Sphingolipids were quantified by UHPLC-MS/MS, while total antioxidant capacity, total oxidant status, and ox
papers.summary: This exploratory study integrated lipidomics, oxidative stress profiling, and transcriptomics from 40 colorectal cancer patients to map sphingolipid remodeling. It found that sphingolipid changes in tumors and serum follow a continuum-like metabolic organization rather than discrete subtypes, linking sphingolipid alterations to systemic oxidative stress. The findings suggest that sphingolipid metabolism in CRC is more interconnected and gradual than previously thought.

papers.title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering o
papers.summary: The authors present CardamomOT, a mechanistic optimal transport framework that infers gene regulatory networks, reconstructs cellular trajectories, and enables generative modeling from single-cell RNA-seq data. It extends their earlier CARDAMOM algorithm by using optimal transport to overcome limitations in temporal ordering and protein dynamics inference. The method aims to establish causal links between regulator activity and target gene responses during processes like differentiation and reprogramming.

papers.title: Systems biology-driven drug repurposing in glioblastoma via antigen and pathway mapping.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with limited treatment options and poor patient survival. This study aimed to identify key genes and altered pathways in GBM and to explore potential drug-repurposing candidates using a systems biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies a systems biology approach to glioblastoma, integrating gene expression and pathway data to identify key altered genes and pathways, then maps these to potential drug-repurposing candidates. It aims to find existing drugs that could be redirected to treat this aggressive brain tumor with limited therapeutic options.

papers.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: Evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species.
papers.abstract: Interventions targeting conserved aging pathways can markedly extend lifespan in model organisms, yet their efficacy declines with increasing organismal complexity. While this phenomenon is well documented, the underlying constraints remain poorly defined. Here, we integrate comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to propose a unifying framework explaining the declining ceiling of lifespan extension. We show that in simple organisms, aging is governed by a limited number of high-leverage pathways, whereas in mammals it emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems c
papers.summary: This review proposes a unifying framework explaining why lifespan-extending interventions that work well in simple organisms lose efficacy in more complex ones. The authors argue that aging shifts from being controlled by a few high-leverage pathways in simple organisms to distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems in mammals, creating a system-level buffering that limits intervention gains.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) to resolve disagreements between methods on a per-edge basis rather than choosing one method or averaging all. The authors also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts, evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified human-mouse shared gene space and uses supervised contrastive learning to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression relationships via a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor-target regulatory interactions, addressing noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts.

papers.title: Single-cell virtual knockout network perturbation prioritizes candidate regulators of beta-cell functional failure in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction is a central feature of type 2 diabetes (T2D), but disease-associated transcriptional changes alone cannot distinguish likely regulatory drivers from secondary stress markers. Single-cell transcriptomics resolves beta-cell heterogeneity across disease states, while virtual-knockout network analysis estimates transcriptional effects after perturbing selected genes. We combined human islet single-cell RNA sequencing, beta-cell functional-state modeling, candidate scoring, scTenifoldKnk virtual knockout, and external validation to prioritize regulators
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell RNA sequencing of human pancreatic islets with virtual-knockout network perturbation (scTenifoldKnk) to distinguish regulatory drivers of beta-cell failure in type 2 diabetes from passive stress markers. By modeling beta-cell functional states and scoring candidate regulators, the authors prioritize genes whose network perturbation effects suggest causal roles in disease progression, validated against external datasets.

papers.title: Evolution, disciplinary integration, and frontiers of multi-omics and single-cell technologies in periodontology: a bibliometric analysis (2000-2025) with an early-2026 frontier update.
papers.abstract: The field of periodontology is undergoing a paradigm shift from traditional microbiology to systems biology, driven by advancements in multi-omics and single-cell technologies. Despite the rapid surge in publications, a Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC)-based bibliometric and scientometric analysis mapping the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of these technologies in periodontal research remains needed. We performed a bibliometric and scientometric analysis of literature published from 2000 to 2025, with records from early 2026 used only as an exploratory frontier update, us
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the evolution of multi-omics and single-cell technologies in periodontology from 2000 to 2025, showing a paradigm shift from traditional microbiology toward systems biology. It identifies emerging research frontiers and provides an early-2026 update on the field's trajectory.

papers.title: Probiogenomics as a Computational Biotechnology Framework: Safety-Gated Genome Analytics for Candidate Probiotic Prioritization and Validation.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing has transformed probiotic discovery into a strain-resolved computational problem, but genome data alone cannot establish probiotic efficacy, complete safety, or regulatory acceptability. This review frames probiogenomics as a safety-gated decision-support framework for candidate probiotic prioritization and validation. The framework integrates strain provenance, genome quality, strain authentication, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance screening, virulence and toxin assessment, plasmid, prophage and mobile-element analysis, undesirable metabolite screening, f
papers.summary: This review proposes probiogenomics as a computational decision-support framework that uses whole-genome sequencing to prioritize and validate probiotic candidates, with safety screening as a mandatory gate. It integrates strain provenance, genome quality, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance, virulence factors, mobile elements, and metabolite screening to guide candidate selection. The authors emphasize that genomic data alone cannot establish efficacy or regulatory acceptability, so the framework is positioned as a filtering and prioritization tool rather than a standalone proof of probiotic benefit.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using an integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics approach. The authors combine toxicology predictions with multi-omics data to identify potential molecular mechanisms linking PFOA exposure to MASLD pathogenesis. The findings suggest PFOA may act as an environmental risk factor for MASLD through systems-level perturbations.
